q: The Radon-Nikodym theorem states that if ν ≪ μ (ν absolutely continuous w.r.t. μ), then:
opts: There exists a measurable f ≥ 0 such that ν(A) = ∫_A f dμ for all measurable A
ν and μ are mutually singular
exp: Radon-Nikodym yields the density dν/dμ (the Radon-Nikodym derivative). It is fundamental in probability (conditional expectation) and ergodic theory (invariant measures).
